data.body:
AC2 NOW SATISFIED - the parametrised table coverage landed as Gerrit 2083 (merged). This was the criterion the completion verifier correctly refused the close on: the suite that originally landed was 32 hand-written per-(edge, surface) cases, and 'checked by a parametrised test over the table' was not true of it.

What landed: tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py::test_every_table_edge_cascades_through_the_real_transition, parametrised over the LIVE _CASCADING_EDGES, driven through rebar.transition rather than through cascade_parent_first. Driving the real surface is the point - the injected-walk unit tests pass for ANY row by construction because the walk is table-agnostic, so only the real path can show a row is WIRED. Proven by mutation: making transition ignore the (closed, open) row fails exactly that case with the message naming the edge. tests/unit/commands/test_lifecycle_cascade.py keeps a table-driven pair pinning each row's eligible-status contract, with a docstring stating plainly that it cannot prove wiring - claiming durability there would have been a tautology dressed as a guard, and my first draft of it was exactly that before I caught it.

Why the tripwire was not enough on its own: test_the_cascading_edge_table_is_unchanged asserts equality against a literal dict, so a fourth row DOES break it and make the author look. But updating that literal is all it forces; nothing then obliges the new row to actually cascade. The two bugs this story descends from, cranial-sulfur-peafowl and paragonite-fruited-minnow, were both 'an edge the cascade did not know about', so a tripwire alone leaves that bug class open. Parametrising over the live table mints a new case on import for any new row.

AC2's WORDING remains imprecise and is recorded here rather than silently ticked: 'every edge exercised for both claim and transition' is not literally satisfiable, because claim only ever moves open -> in_progress and cannot walk the two closed-source rows. A test now asserts that narrowness deliberately, so a future second claim edge is noticed on purpose. 15 tests pass in the unit tier.
